newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: CONTEMPT CHARGE LIKELY FOR CHANNEL TEN
The New South Wales Director of Public Prosecutions has recommended Channel Ten be charged with contempt of court after a Supreme Court murder trial was aborted last week.
The trial of 27-year-old David John Zammitt was aborted on Friday when a Channel Ten news story covered what happened when the jury left the court-room.
DPP, Nicholas Cowdrey Q-C, has recommended a contempt charge be laid against the station, with the final decision in the hands of Attorney-General, Jeff Shaw.
Mr Zammitt has pleaded not guilty to the murder of a service station owner while she deposited money at a Summer Hill bank in 1994.
AUSTUDY APPLICATIONS TO BE REPROCESSED
Thousands of Austudy applications are to be urgently reprocessed, after the Federal Government admitted its reforms were too harsh.
Employment, Education and Training Minister, Amanda Vanstone, says the process used to assess applicants disadvantaged some students who were genuinely entitled to Austudy.
Senator Vanstone's instructed her Department to re-assess all applications, and contact all affected students.
She says she deeply regrets the inconvenience caused, but expects to have the problem cleared up in two to three weeks.
MCGRATH UNREPENTENT FOR GAY POLICE COMMENTS
Victorian Police Minister, Bill McGrath, says he's surprised by the reaction to his comments on homosexuals in the force.
He says he stands by his reservations about gay and lesbian officers, and has a right to express his personal opinions.
He's also been defended by the Premier, who says the Minister was simply being honest.
Jeff Kennett says Opposition calls for Mr McGrath's sacking are ridiculous.
Mr McGrath says, as far as he's concerned, the matter is over.
TAX REFORM LOBBY GROUP FORMED
Pressure is growing on the Federal Government to reform the tax system, with the formation of a new alliance today.
The Tax Reform Forum is a collaboration between the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the Business Council, and the Australian Council of Social Service.
ACOSS President, Robert Fitzgerald, says business and welfare groups have different interests, but are united in calling for tax reform.
He says the forum is not simply about lobbying for a goods and services tax.
But he says it aims to set out an argument for taxation reform, which will allow political parties to make their own decisions.
CARR COOL ON EDUCATION OMBUDSMAN IDEA
New South Wales Premier, Bob Carr, has distanced himself from any move to establish an education ombudsman.
Mr Carr says he'll wait on the recommendations of the Wood Royal Commission before committing to an ombudsman, to handle complaints against teachers and schools.
The Premier says his preferred approach is to use existing mechanisms rather than create well-paid new jobs in the bureaucracy.
He says it's the Department of School Education's job to deliver education and to protect students, and it should become better at that.
GREENPEACE STILL SEARCHING FOR NUKE SHIP
Greenpeace says it's resumed the search off southern Tasmania for a vessel carrying radioactive waste from France to Japan.

The British ship, Pacific Teal, is thought to be close to entering Australian waters with its shipment of plutonium waste. This morning, an aircraft carrying a Greenpeace representative and a photographer left Hobart to search for the vessel, but was forced to turn back because of poor visibility.
The search co-ordinator, Damon Moglan, says they're now trying again.
Mr Moglan says the search will continue for a few days if necessary.
WA GOLFER CLUBHOUSE LEADER
A six under 66 by West Australian golfer, Chris Gray, has him clubhouse leader following his first round in the Canon Golf Challenge at Sydney's Terrey Hills Course.
A shot behind and still on the course after 13 holes is England's Ben Jackson along with Lucas Parsons who's completed 11 holes.
At four under and also in the clubhouse is Australian Masters champion Peter Lonard, Peter Senior, David Smail and Grant Kenny.
